claim.why_it_matters: Same defect as p.1178: the flowchart is flattened to a bag of labels with all four 'yes' edges heaped at the end and no boxes, arrows or branch targets. The distinctive structure of this figure — that the yes-exits of Condition-1 and Condition-2 BOTH re-enter at [Evaluate condition-3], which is what encodes '(condition-1 OR NOT condition-2) AND ...' — is completely unrecoverable from the transcription.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED on both sides, independently, at 300 dpi. PDF side (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1179/spec_p1179.png, printed folio 1149): the page carries a full flowchart and nothing else but the running head and the ISO footer. I traced every edge in the render and the claim's topology is correct in every particular: [Evaluate condition-1] feeds decision (Condition-1 true); its 'yes' runs right and turns down a right-hand channel; its 'no' drops into [Evaluate condition-2] -> decision (Condition-2 false); that decision's 'yes' also runs right and MERGES into the same right-hand channel, and the merged channel enters the top of [Evaluate condition-3]; the 'no' exit of (Condition-2 false) continues straight down a LEFT-hand channel. [Evaluate condition-3] -> (Condition-3 false): 'yes' runs left into the left channel, 'no' drops to [Evaluate condition-4] -> (Condition-4 false): 'yes' runs left into the left channel, 'no' drops with an arrowhead to 'Truth value is true'. The left channel ends in an arrowhead over 'Truth value is false'. In the printed glyphs, 'false' and 'true' in the two terminals are each underlined (a visible rule under the word, not italic/bold). I also verified the figure's IDENTITY rather than taking it on trust, because the caption is not on this page. Evaluating the charted logic: (c1 true) OR (c2 false) reaches condition-3; c2 true-and-c1-false yields false; then c3 must not be false and c4 must not be false. That is exactly '(condition-1 OR NOT condition-2) AND condition-3 AND condition-4' — the D.10 caption. Rendering p.1178 confirms the layout: p.1178 carries a DIFFERENT, three-condition chart whose logic is 'condition-1 OR (condition-2 AND condition-3)' (i.e. Figure D.9), and the bold caption 'Figure D.10 — Evaluation of (condition-1 OR NOT condition-2) AND condition-3 AND condition-4' is printed at its foot, one page ahead of the diagram it names. The claim's parenthetical is therefore accurate. Markdown side (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 47590-47641, anchor ): the quoted text is verbatim and complete — nothing was omitted from the quote and nothing structural exists on an adjacent line. The whole page is 24 bare label fragments. Every box outline, every arrow, every branch target and both channel merges are absent, and the four 'yes' labels are heaped together after all four 'no' labels rather than sitting on their own edges. This is not wrapping, page furniture, or formatting. A flowchart's meaning IS its topology, and none of it survived. Worse than the claim states, the flattened label ORDER positively asserts something false: read linearly it says 'Condition-2 false / no / Evaluate condition-3', whereas in the PDF the 'no' exit of (Condition-2 false) goes to 'Truth value is false' and it is the two YES exits of Condition-1 and Condition-2 that converge on [Evaluate condition-3]. A reader reconstructing D.10 from the markdown would derive the wrong Boolean. The defect is also demonstrably fixable rather than inherent: the same transcription already carries a Unicode box-drawing flowchart plus a '> **Figure notes ...**' prose block for Figure D.9 (lines ~47498-47538). Pages 1178 and 1179 simply never received that treatment. No ASCII art and no figure-notes block exists anywhere for D.10. Only two nits, neither of which weakens the finding: the printed underlining of 'false'/'true' is not lost — it is approximated as bold (**false** / **true**); and the claim's severity framing 'same defect as p.1178' is right, but p.1179 is the strictly worse of the pair because its topology is non-linear and the flattened order misleads.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with two refinements. (1) Figure identity is correct but worth stating precisely: the diagram on p.1179 IS Figure D.10 — 'Evaluation of (condition-1 OR NOT condition-2) AND condition-3 AND condition-4' — confirmed by evaluating the charted logic; its bold caption is printed at the foot of p.1178, one page ahead of the diagram (p.1178 itself carries the three-condition Figure D.9 chart, whose logic is condition-1 OR (condition-2 AND condition-3)). (2) The loss is worse than 'unrecoverable': the flattened label order in specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 47590-47641 actively implies a FALSE linear cascade 'Condition-2 false -> no -> Evaluate condition-3', when the printed 'no' exit of (Condition-2 false) goes to the left channel and terminates at 'Truth value is false'. It is the YES exits of Condition-1 and Condition-2 that merge into the right-hand channel feeding [Evaluate condition-3]. Everything else in the claim holds: all boxes, arrows, channel merges and branch targets are absent, and the four 'yes' labels are heaped after all four 'no' labels. The underlining of 'false'/'true' is the one thing not lost — it survives as bold. Remedy: transcribe the chart as a Unicode box-drawing block plus a '> **Figure notes (Figure D.10 ...)**' paragraph, exactly as the same file already does for Figure D.9 at lines ~47498-47538; neither exists for D.10 today.
